title: review: V1-V3: next_goal after a model close, next_goal enabled_at reset, CLI shutdown joins the ship thread
spec:
From the final verification of goal/T-1667 (2026-10-07); superseded T-1704 (its base predated goal/T-1667).
V1 medium planner_runs.py ~283/285: next_goal fires only when pipeline.closed_at is set, which only routine_close stamps
   (~1654). Stamp closed_at wherever result.goal_closed is posted (model-close path too), and in next_goal fall back to the
   goal_closed event time when closed_at is missing. test_next_goal_after_model_close.
V2 low planner_runs.py ~254-272: delete .orchestrator/next_goal_state.json when next_goal is seen disabled, so off-then-on
   does not make goals closed while off eligible. test_reenable_resets_enabled_at.
V3 low daemon.py ~2110: the CLI daemon passes a stop Event that is never set; after Ctrl-C the non-daemon ship thread keeps
   running while daemon.lock is released. Set the Event in main's finally, then ship.join_threads(timeout) (bounded, log if it
   times out) before releasing the lock. test_cli_shutdown_stops_ship_thread_before_lock_release.
Run: PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_next_goal tests.test_daemon tests.test_ship. Commit on the task branch.
acceptance: V1-V3 each have their named test and it passes

result.summary: V1, V2 and V3 are each implemented with their named tests (test_next_goal_after_model_close, test_reenable_resets_enabled_at, test_cli_shutdown_stops_ship_thread_before_lock_release). All changes stay within the listed scope. I did not run the suites. The one real concern is the stale-snapshot overwrite in _stamp_closed_at.

comments.issue: _stamp_closed_at writes pipeline from the all_tasks snapshot read before bus.locked(). If another writer changed pipeline fields in between, bus.update overwrites them with stale values. Re-read the goal with bus.get(goal['id']) inside the lock before copying pipeline.

The ship thread is joined for at most 60s, then the lock is released while it may still be alive. This is bounded and logged as the spec asks, but a new daemon could start a second ship run. Acceptable per spec.

The test uses a fake thread that waits on the stop event, so it proves the event is set before the lock is released. It does not exercise a real ship thread started via ship.start. Adequate for the acceptance criterion.
